title: BSC Project: Data Status and Coverage

pages.title:
BSC Project:
Data Status and Coverage

blocks.text: Report date: 21 September 2026    Audience: Product owner and project team

The agreed data preparation, read-access setup and independent review are complete, with an additional set of manufacturer lithium-battery sources. The project now has traceable inputs and source evidence for the next build stage. Clear gaps remain in lithium-battery models, application scenarios and complete operating conditions, so the full external-data requirement cannot yet be considered satisfied.
Problem the project is intended to solve

The planned system will combine a user's description of site conditions, product and site documents uploaded for the case, queryable records and analysis tools to produce evidence-backed assessments. It should distinguish known facts, inference and unknowns, then use applicable UNSW procedures to suggest actions, further checks and escalation. The first version will use general analysis plus case-specific inputs rather than assume prior knowledge of every device.

blocks.text: Current stage

Completed work is limited to data preparation and bounded review. RAG retrieval, the target database, Qwen integration, and system or model performance testing were not carried out in these preparation runs. [1][2][3]
Reading guide: page 2 covers data types; pages 3–6 cover breadth; page 7 explains usability and progress; page 8 lists gaps and reference locations.

The 300 original sources total 112,415,624,680 bytes, or about 112.42 GB. One archive may contain many experimental members, and one battery sample may generate millions of time points. Data volume therefore cannot be judged by dividing gigabytes by the number of index entries. [1]

blocks.text: Originals, archive members, worksheets, objects and rows are different nested levels and must not be added together as a total sample count. 112.42 GB is about 104.70 GiB; the difference is only the display unit.

Large data remain in their native formats with traceable read methods so that specific fields or slices can be loaded when needed. A small index may therefore point to a very large measurement set. Passing format checks also does not make every experiment applicable to the current device.

Material spans eight knowledge domains, plus comparative references from other laboratories, universities and industry. It supports explanation and analysis; product parameters, site procedures and test conditions still require case-specific matching. [1][4]

rows: Physics and chemistry foundations
DOE, NASA and others: charge, power, energy, heat, capacity and battery health.
Does not establish every battery's reaction kinetics, thermal parameters or lifetime model.
Battery and system engineering
Manufacturer data and foxBMS examples: cells, modules, protection and chargers.
Match the exact model, version and system configuration.
Measurement and analysis methods
NASA, CALCE and TRI data; NIST measurement principles.
Units, signs, sampling, missing values and calibration may differ by dataset.
Anomaly and failure evidence
UNSW, SafeWork NSW and experimental failure evidence: signs and observations.
Observations do not prove cause, probability or time to failure.
Lifecycle practice
MIT, UNSW and NSW EPA: charging, discharging, storage, checks, maintenance and disposal.
General practice cannot replace manufacturer limits, safety information or site controls.
Institutional procedures and applicable rules
UNSW risk and safe-work procedures; transport and standards references.
The site supplies activity-specific procedures and approvals; check applicable versions.
Emergency and escalation paths
Public UNSW and SafeWork NSW guidance.
Confirm this lab's responsible people, phone numbers, emergency cards and routes at use.
Experimental and method validation
NASA, CALCE and TRI protocols, field/read conventions and validation inputs.
Inputs do not prove that a tool is implemented or a model is effective.

blocks.text: How authority should be judged

Manufacturer evidence supports its named products; UNSW and local institutions explain relevant procedures; research datasets support analysis under stated test conditions. These roles are not interchangeable. Even authoritative sources require version, permission and applicability checks.

Other universities and laboratories offer comparisons where local procedures lack detail. State their original context; do not present them as UNSW-approved. Some DOE battery-management material concerns storage or lead-acid batteries and cannot apply directly to every lithium battery.

Lithium batteries are the primary application focus. After the latest preparation batch, mainstream lithium-ion chemistries have clearer background and product evidence, although depth varies by chemistry. “Available” below means relevant evidence exists; it does not mean complete operating parameters or a complete market catalogue. [3][5]

rows: LCO — lithium cobalt oxide
One exact Saft protected battery-pack model with a chemistry declaration and some operating parameters.
The document is historical and cannot establish chemistry or operating conditions for other cells.
NMC or NCM — nickel manganese cobalt
Exact LG Energy Solution pouch models and related research data.
Complete charge/discharge conditions and approved specifications for target models.
NCA — nickel cobalt aluminium
Murata cylindrical models with explicit manufacturer-catalogue chemistry and basic parameters.
Current availability and complete model operating conditions.
LFP — lithium iron phosphate
Exact LG and Lishen cells, plus CATL, EVE and BYD material at different product levels.
Information from one family or system cannot be applied to every LFP battery.
LMO — lithium manganese oxide
DOE overview, research material and product-family background.
No verified chemistry binding to an exact commercial model.
LTO — lithium titanate anode
Toshiba SCiB family declaration and exact module records.
Exact cell models and corresponding cathode information; LTO identifies the anode material.
Primary lithium
One specific Murata CR2032 coin-cell example.
A broader primary-lithium overview and more models; rechargeable-battery charging conditions do not apply.
Special or emerging chemistries
Tracked as a separate scope, with no specific chemistry selected yet.
Solid-state, rechargeable lithium-metal and other systems should be added only for an identified use case.

blocks.text: Forms and system levels

Manufacturer evidence now contains exact labels for cylindrical, prismatic and pouch forms. The model names and dimensions of the added Panasonic prismatic cells are confirmed, but their catalogue does not declare model-level chemistry, so it remains unknown.

Coverage also reaches modules, battery packs, racks, protection/BMS functions, and one manufacturer-defined battery-pack and charger combination. Knowing that a device has protection does not establish its thresholds, firmware logic or cause of failure.
The LG catalogue also contains NCMA material labels. They are preserved as stated by the source and are not automatically merged into NMC or NCA.

The project currently identifies 66 exact product labels, 65 with an identified manufacturer. These products include cells, modules, racks and kits. Brand names, dimensions, family names and experimental sample IDs are not counted as exact commercial product labels. [3][6]

blocks.text: The 66 labels comprise 34 existing labels plus 32 non-duplicate labels from the latest preparation batch. A further 10 families, 13 series and 248 research-sample identity groups are stored separately and are not included in the 66.

Manufacturer count is not a coverage percentage. BYD Blade Battery remains family-level material and is not included among the exact labels above. Historical catalogues prove information only for their documented versions, not current sale status or procurement interchangeability.

Support varies substantially by scenario. The table shows what current evidence can support and what is still needed before handling a real case; it does not indicate that a model has been tested in these scenarios. [4][5]

rows: UNSW teaching and laboratories
Public safety, risk-planning and escalation references; experimental data and product examples.
Risk assessment, safe-work procedure, assets and current emergency contacts for the activity.
Portable devices
Model identities and basic parameters for cylindrical, pouch and prismatic cells.
The actual device's battery pack, BMS, charger and user manual.
Power tools
One Bosch manufacturer-defined battery-pack and charger combination.
Target tool code, site temperature and mode; evidence cannot be extended to other brands.
Light mobility
General guidance on charging location and anomaly recognition.

Energy storage systems
Module or rack examples from Samsung, CATL, GS Yuasa and others.
Complete system design, wiring, cooling, and site electrical and fire conditions.

blocks.text: Coverage from procurement to end of life

Procurement and identity checks now record manufacturer, model, version and source, but authenticity, current availability and compatibility still need confirmation. Some charging and discharging sources provide voltage, current, temperature or time conditions. Charge conditions used in a capacity test must remain experimental context and must not automatically become recommended operating limits.

General principles exist for storage, use and maintenance, but most models still lack complete state-of-charge, temperature, duration and maintenance requirements. Conditioned ageing data can support future method development; a general battery-health estimation tool has not been implemented or validated.

Transport, disposal and anomaly escalation have branching guidance. Actual transport still requires the applicable rule version, battery condition, quantity and packaging to be checked. Disposal and emergency response must follow current campus or jurisdictional routes. Existing material cannot determine the cause, probability or time to failure for a new incident.
Case-specific input is a normal part of the product workflow. Gaps in public evidence require later source work. The two should be managed separately.
Original-file processing and use

All 300 original files have a registration and disposition result. The previously unresolved groups of 60 and 7 files now each have a processing or restriction decision. A recorded outcome does not mean every full text was extracted or may be placed in a knowledge base. The 300 originals are classified as follows. [1]

rows: Conditionally usable
Select under each source's permission, attribution, version and use conditions.
Split by specific action
For example, numerical analysis and placing explanatory source text into a model have different conditions.
Local LLM or RAG use not allowed
Registration and review records are retained, but the files cannot be directly imported for that use.
Not selected for the current minimal build set
Not selected does not mean invalid or permanently prohibited.

blocks.text: All 207 candidates have semantic clarification

Earlier document processing extracted 673 numerically related records, of which 207 required additional context review. All 207 now have semantic clarification: 92 are source-bounded parameters, experimental conditions or rules, and 115 serve other roles such as identifiers, references or layout. The previous unresolved count is now zero. The remaining 466 retain prior review results and were not comprehensively re-reviewed in that pass. [2]

Use status for the same 207 records is separately classified as 65 conditionally allowed, 84 not selected for the minimal set, and 58 not allowed for local RAG. This classification counts records, while the table above counts original files; the figures cannot be subtracted or combined. Semantic clarification does not upgrade permissions, and the 92 records are not automatically device operating instructions.
How the lithium-product increment can be used

The added product batch contains 42 records and 174 fact fields, each checked against its source, unit and condition. Fact fields are specific items such as model, capacity and voltage. Of these, 40 records and 164 fields were selected as the incremental preparation set for later internal queries; two restricted reused Molicel records were not selected. The 40 comprise 32 exact product labels and 8 family records. They do not represent all usable project data. [3]

Current deliverables include actual document content, sourced facts, read-access paths for experimental data and validation material. RAG ingestion of source text, model training, external redistribution and server transfer are separate uses and cannot be inferred as permitted merely because material was parsed or publicly accessible.
Items still incomplete or not safe to guess include the full text of one copy-controlled summary, units for some special MAT fields, and product- and site-specific applicability conditions.

The data-preparation deliverables can be accepted within their stated scope. Traceable entry points now exist for mainstream lithium-battery foundations, several product levels and large experimental datasets. Broader model and scenario coverage remains incomplete. Passing data-preparation checks does not mean that the analysis tools, database, RAG or Qwen performance have been accepted.
Public material still needed

Priorities are an exact LMO product, a named light-mobility battery-pack and charger combination, a broader primary-lithium overview, and complete charge, discharge, storage and maintenance conditions for target products. Gaps remain in A123 manufacturer material, specific Samsung cells, a complete BYD cell model and the full EVE LF280K specification. Special chemistries should be scoped only after the intended use is identified.
Three decisions for the next stage

First, select the initial representative tasks and their input requirements, and turn “what the evidence is sufficient to answer” into testable criteria. Second, organise knowledge text, product facts and native experimental data through a use-specific manifest that preserves source, conditions, knowns and unknowns; do not bulk-import whole folders. Third, once system construction starts, validate retrieval, numerical tools and model answers separately rather than use data-preparation checks as a proxy for system performance.
Review and execution record

The latest lithium preparation batch received author processing, independent item-by-item audit and coordinator review. The 297 existing identity records, 42 product records and 40 query-preparation records each have corresponding checks. All 16 final handover checks passed, but they do not constitute a physical experiment or a site-safety conclusion.

Disclosed execution issues include a historical mistaken RData dependency installation with limited recovery evidence, and correction of restricted-page rendering. The latest preparation batch also involved quarantine after discovering ULRI automated-access restrictions, withdrawal of an HTML response mistakenly treated as a PDF, and a policy rejection of temporary render cleanup. Detailed records are retained; these events must not be described as never having occurred. [1][3]
